title: Why Sleep Is the Brain's Best Friend

paragraphs.text: The human brain performs its most important maintenance work while the body rests. During deep sleep, the brain clears away metabolic waste products that accumulate during waking hours, a process scientists liken to a nightly street-sweeping service.

Memory consolidation also depends heavily on sleep. Researchers have shown that information learned during the day is replayed and strengthened during the night. Students who sleep well after studying consistently outperform those who sacrifice rest for extra revision.

Yet modern life conspires against adequate rest. Blue light from screens suppresses melatonin, the hormone that signals sleepiness. The resulting sleep deficit has been linked to impaired attention, weakened immunity, and even long-term cognitive decline.

The remedy is disarmingly simple: protect your sleep schedule as rigorously as you would a deadline. Keep consistent hours, dim the lights in the evening, and keep screens out of the bedroom. Your brain, quite literally, will thank you.
